doc.title: Cedar Walton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Blakey never read music; his deference to Billy Eckstine
summary: Blakey had no written drum parts, played with Eckstine and acted demure when Walton met Eckstine with him; Walton adds stories of Eckstine's toughness, his knot and his not joining the Rat Pack.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: When you, when you wrote for him uh … You didn't write anything for him.
Yeah, I wrote Mosaic. Well, I mean …
I mean in the sense you didn't write any parts for him.

Oh, no, no, no. That was out of the question. No, he, he went through his whole uh musical uh career uh, it was no reading involved. He played with Billy Eckstine. He took me over to meet uh Billy Eckstine one night, and that was a … that was the first time I'd seen Art act real uh kind of demure [chuckles] in the presence of Mr. B. That was a …
Well, Billy had to be a bad, had to be a tough guy.

Oh yeah. They, they, they, they had fights and physical fights when he came through the South, when he had Dexter and all of them, playing to uh divided audiences, and so I'm just … this is hearsay I'm tellin' you. But I believe it, though.
But to command the respect of the, of the kind of men he had in his band …

Dizzy Gillespie uh, uh, uh noted that on one of his interviews. He understood the music – he was talkin' 'bout Billy Eckstine – and how to present it and plus he could sing, he was handsome. He [inaudible-overlapping voices] …
He could knock your ass out.
That too. And he even had a knot named after him, the Billy Eckstine Knot.
You mean like in a collar?

A collar. Yeah. Knot in the collar. So uh, I'm told when he was asked to join the Rat Pack, you know, with uh Sinatra and those people … I think uh Sammy Davis ended up joinin'. But uh Billy would never uh take part in anything like that. I don't think he had to, it wasn't the style of, that wasn't his style, I don't think. So uh, that was uh … Kimery: So … ready?
